mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved monotonically from -18.0% (t-3w) to -10.9% (t-0w), a 7.1 percentage point recovery trend. This sustained upward trajectory in retail mobility indicates consumer confidence is rebuilding week-on-week. Absent a shock, this trend will continue, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks relative to the baseline period.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 7.1 points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the mean over the last 28 days (-13.4%).

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility remains elevated (58.4% at t-0w) and has stabilized above 36% for four consecutive weeks, indicating sustained outdoor activity preference. This behavioral shift reflects a durable substitution away from indoor retail toward outdoor recreation. If PARKS remains above 50%, outdoor preference will suppress RETAIL_REC recovery, keeping it below the prior four-week mean.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains above 50% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the prior 28-day mean despite PARKS remaining above 50%.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has declined from -13.3% (t-3w and t-2w) to -21.4% (t-1w), then recovered slightly to -17.6% (t-0w). This volatility in workplace attendance signals uncertainty in return-to-office patterns. When WORKPLACES falls more than 5 points week-on-week, commuting-dependent retail footfall (transit-adjacent shops) contracts, suppressing RETAIL_REC growth over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES declines more than 5 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell 7.1 points from t-2w to t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises by more than 2 percentage points in the week following a WORKPLACES decline of 5+ points.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT stations remain severely depressed (-26.7% at t-0w, stable around -26% for four weeks), indicating public transport avoidance persists. GROCERY_PHARM has strengthened to +8.0% (t-0w), showing essential-trip mobility is robust. The combination of weak transit and strong essential shopping signals consumers are making targeted trips only. This bifurcation suppresses discretionary RETAIL_REC visits, keeping recovery muted over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds -10% (the current level) while TRANSIT remains below -25% and GROCERY_PHARM remains above +5%.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from +5.4% (t-3w) to +2.7% (t-0w), a 2.7 point drop, signaling residents are spending less time at home and more time outside. This shift out of residential space, combined with RETAIL_REC's steady improvement, indicates policy restrictions on indoor gathering are loosening. Over the next week, this regime shift will accelerate RETAIL_REC recovery as indoor retail capacity constraints ease.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines more than 2 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell 2.7 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to improve in the week following a RESIDENTIAL decline of 2+ points, or RESIDENTIAL rebounds above +4%.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has surged to 58.4% and remains elevated, consistent with mid-winter (June in Melbourne) outdoor recreation preference. RETAIL_REC at -10.9% reflects seasonal substitution of indoor retail for outdoor parks. This seasonal pattern is self-reinforcing: as winter progresses toward early spring (next four weeks), outdoor activity will remain elevated, suppressing indoor retail recovery below the prior four-week mean.
candidate_trigger: PARKS above 50% for three consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the prior 28-day mean (-13.4%) while PARKS remains above 50% for the entire period.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has strengthened consistently from +4.0% (t-3w) to +8.0% (t-0w), a 4 percentage point gain, indicating essential shopping trips are accelerating. This rise in essential mobility crowds out discretionary retail visits. When GROCERY_PHARM exceeds +7%, consumers are allocating their mobility budget to essential errands, leaving less capacity for RETAIL_REC. Over the next two weeks, elevated GROCERY_PHARM will constrain RETAIL_REC growth.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC improves by more than 3 percentage points over the next two weeks while GROCERY_PHARM remains above +7%.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES has recovered from -21.4% (t-1w) to -17.6% (t-0w), a 3.8 point rebound, while TRANSIT remains flat at -26.7%. This decoupling signals workers are returning to offices via private transport, not public transit. As workplace attendance stabilizes and private commuting patterns solidify, retail footfall in transit-adjacent zones will remain suppressed. RETAIL_REC will fail to recover to the prior four-week mean over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves by 2+ points while TRANSIT remains below -25%
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES recovered 3.8 points, TRANSIT flat at -26.7%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the prior 28-day mean while WORKPLACES improves and TRANSIT remains below -25%.
